items.text:
China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct
November 22, 2026
It was supposed to be a breakthrough year. The Philippines had intended to set up a code of conduct with China for the South China Sea during its 2026 ASEAN presidency. However, at the summit in Manila in mid-November they had to abandon their goal. Some 80% of the text had been negotiated, declared Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, but the key areas of dispute had remained unsolved.
Much more than diplomatic wording is at stake. The South China Sea is one of the world's most important shipping routes, it is rich in fishing grounds and may harbor significant oil and gas reserves. Primarily, however, it's a region of strategic competition: With its so-called Nine-Dash Line (often drawn in red), China claims a large portion of the sea. Its claims overlap with those of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.
A code of conduct is to set up rules for parties dealing with one another and prevent incidents at sea from escalating. However, opinions differ, particularly with regard to its binding nature and its geographic scope.
"The basic problem with establishing such a code of conduct is that China is supremely powerful and has no real interest in a legally binding agreement," said political scientist Andreas Ufen, Southeast Asia expert at the German Institute of Global and Area Studies (GIGA). Beijing had little incentive to impose restrictions on itself as long as it was able to pursue its interests in the region even without such an agreement, Ufen told DW.
Mere recommendations or legally binding set of rules?
The Paracel Islands serve as an example of just how difficult the unresolved issues are. In China, the group of islands is known as Xisha, in Vietnam as Hoang-Sa. Hanoi apparently wants to include them in the code's geographic scope, but China rejects this. An agreement within the ASEAN framework could indirectly affect the territorial claims of the parties involved.
"A fundamental problem is that so far there's no consensus on whether the code of conduct should be legally binding," said Felix Heiduk, head of research division Asia at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP). China and the ASEAN nations have been negotiating an agreement for 12 years without major progress so far.
There were reservations about such a treaty not only in China but also in other ASEAN countries. They would subsequently have to ratify a legally binding agreement under international law in their own countries. A non-binding code of conduct, by contrast, would be little more than a voluntary declaration of intent, Ufen told DW.
The definition of an "incident" is controversial as well. Are coast guard missions with use of water cannons included? Or blockades of supply vessels? Or is the code only applicable when military force is involved? This will determine which actions will be covered by the regulations in the future.
"These are by no means just technical details. Their clarification determines to a great extent whether the code of conduct will in fact be effective or will ultimately remain only a non-binding declaration of intent," Heiduk said. An agreement without valid commitments would bring about little change.
Diverging interests
Ufen views China's attitude as a strategic calculation. "I believe that China is interested in keeping the conflict simmering, so to speak, without having to commit itself to a truly binding legal regulation," he said. In this way, Beijing could strengthen its position in the South China Sea without limiting its room for maneuver.
At the same time there are also diverging interests within the ASEAN group. The 11 member states are by no means united. The Philippines and Vietnam are particularly vocal in their opposition to China. Malaysia and Indonesia pursue a more restrained approach. Cambodia and Laos have close economic ties with Beijing and don't have any territorial claims in the South China Sea.
"From the start of the negotiations, the lack of unity within ASEAN has been a problem. In a way, it's a permanent obstacle," Heiduk said. The group makes decisions based on the consensus principle, which basically means that every member state can block a unified position. Recurring confrontations between China and the Philippines exacerbated the problem by undermining trust and making it more difficult to reach compromises.
Ufen also believes that diverging interests are a key impediment. "Reconciling them is extremely difficult," he said. China could take advantage of the discord. Beijing preferred bilateral negotiations with individual countries rather than dealing with an entire, united group of nations.
Fundamental conflicts unresolved
A study published by the Singapore-based Yusof Ishak Institute (ISEAS)reaches similar conclusions. Not only China but internal divisions within ASEAN stalled negotiations. The authors warn against exclusively relying on a comprehensive, legally binding treaty. Initially, partial agreements — for example, on crisis communication, rescue operations at sea or maritime environment protection — could be a first step. Developing the 2002 agreement on a non-binding Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea could also be an intermediate step.
Ufen doubts whether Beijing is interested in a binding result. "For this reason, I can't really imagine that China has a real interest in a code of conduct that includes legally binding regulations," he said.
Heiduk warns against overestimating the significance of a potential agreement. "Even if the code of conduct was signed at some point, in whichever shape, that would in no way solve the conflict in the South China Sea," he said. The code could regulate how to handle incidents, but it could not eliminate territorial disputes and competing claims to maritime areas.

The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract at the end of
items.text:
'Not the right time' - Fernandes pauses Man Utd contract talks
- Published
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future.
The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract at the end of the season, though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028.
He was left out of the side under previous manager Michael Carrick but says he has no issues at the club and has chosen to stay at Old Trafford despite offers elsewhere in recent seasons.
He told Sky Sports:, external "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.
"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.
"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.
"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here."
United chief executive Omar Berrada recently spoke about Fernandes' contract situation, saying: "It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private."
Fernandes has scored 75 Premier League goals since signing from Sporting in 2020 and last season set a record for the most assists in a Premier League season.
His form has tailed off this season in a poor start for the club as a whole.
United are 19th in the Premier League table going into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge against rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon.
"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season," Fernandes said.
"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.
"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games."
- 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game 
  - Published2 hours ago
No fallout with Carrick
Fernandes was dropped for the Premier League defeat by Bournemouth last month after being critical of United's approach in their heavy defeat against Como in the Champions League.
But Fernandes says he did not fall out with Carrick, who was sacked on 12 November.
"The manager came to speak to me before the Bournemouth game, to say: 'Look, I'm not going to start you tomorrow. There's nothing to do with the words of Como, I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there's nothing to do with that'," Fernandes said.

items.text:
A leftist Berlin 'Super PAC' shakes up German politics
November 22, 2026
Red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.
The Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.
Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.
Content creation, sharing, networking, campaigning
Neunund20 currently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" issues.
Users with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of New York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.
And there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer says physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.
The Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.
Super PAC-style campaigning is new in Germany
The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.
For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting new type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.
But many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.
Haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.
That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.
"We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles."
Stemming the rise of far-right AfD with digital know-how
The AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.
The social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's new military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.
Haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he said.
Agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer says that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.
Big-tent parties in Germany in decline for decades
Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.
"It is an omission of the parties," he said. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open."
The center-left and center-right big-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.
Party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist

Mikel Arteta said: “Obviously it’s not good David had to come off but at the moment I don’t know [the prognosis]. He will have an MRI tomorrow. We will have more information tomorrow. But we know how important David is to us.”

items.title: Gukesh vs Sindarov: The youngest World Chess Championship in history
items.summary:
Gukesh vs Sindarov: The youngest World Chess Championship in history
India’s Gukesh defends his title against Uzbekistan’s Sindarov in up to 14 games in Geneva from November 22.
India’s Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his world chess title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland,
items.text:
Gukesh vs Sindarov: The youngest World Chess Championship in history
India’s Gukesh defends his title against Uzbekistan’s Sindarov in up to 14 games in Geneva from November 22.
India’s Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his world chess title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland, from November 22 to December 12.
The match, at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny on the outskirts of Geneva, will be played over a maximum of 14 classical games. The first player to reach 7½ points will be crowned world champion.
Both players will be 20 when the first game begins on November 24, making it the youngest world championship match in history.
The road to the crown
The official programme opens with a media day and opening ceremony on November 22. The first game is on November 24, and the 14th and final classical game is scheduled for December 11.
A win earns one point, a draw half a point and a loss none. Players have 120 minutes for their first 40 moves, then 30 minutes for the rest of the game, with 30 seconds added per move from move 41. Draw offers are not allowed before move 40.
If the score is tied at 7–7 after 14 games, the title will be decided on December 12 through tiebreaks at faster time controls, starting with four rapid games.
The players will share a $2.5m prize fund. Each earns $200,000 per game won, and the rest is split equally.
One will leave Geneva with the crown.
The contenders: India vs Uzbekistan
Gukesh made history in December 2024, when he defeated China’s Ding Liren in Singapore to become the youngest undisputed world champion, aged 18. Geneva will be his first title defence.
Sindarov won the 2025 FIDE World Cup, then the 2026 Candidates Tournament in Cyprus, where he went unbeaten and scored 10 points from 14 games. Victory in Geneva would make him the first undisputed world champion from Uzbekistan. His compatriot Rustam Kasimdzhanov won FIDE’s version of the title in 2004, when the crown was split.
Sindarov arrives with the stronger record against his opponent. He leads their classical head-to-head 2–0 with one draw, and Gukesh has never beaten him in a classical game.
World champions through history
Since Wilhelm Steinitz became the first recognised world chess champion in 1886, 21 players have held the title over 140 years.
The championship’s history reflects the changing balance of power in chess. European masters dominated its early decades, with Germany’s Emanuel Lasker holding the title for a record 27 years, from 1894 to 1921.
After the second world war, Soviet players took over. From 1948 until 1972, every world champion came from the Soviet Union, beginning with Mikhail Botvinnik.
That run ended in 1972, when American Bobby Fischer defeated Boris Spassky in a match that became a defining moment of the Cold War. The title returned to Soviet hands in 1975, starting the era of Anatoly Karpov and Garry Kasparov, whose rivalry shaped chess for the next two decades.
In 1993, Kasparov broke away from FIDE, chess’s governing body, to form the Professional Chess Association. Two rival world titles existed until they were reunified in 2006. Since then, the crown has passed to India’s Viswanathan Anand, Norway’s Magnus Carlsen, China’s Ding Liren and, in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju.
The Soviet Union and Russia have produced nine of the 22 champions. India has produced two, Anand and Gukesh, and 11 other countries have each produced one.
In Geneva, either Gukesh will join the small group of players who have defended the title, or Sindarov will add Uzbekistan’s name to the list of undisputed champions.

items.text:
Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
Published November 21, 2026last updated November 22, 2026
What you need to know
- The IG Metall union is launching another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues to escalate
- The water level in the Rhine River is rising again after a long period during which shipping was hindered
- German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is kicking off an Africa trip that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya
- Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig wants to tighten laws on femicide
This is a roundup of the top stories from and about Germany on the weekend of Saturday, November 21, and Sunday, November 22, 2026:
Justice Minister Hubig wants harsher penalities for femicide
Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig says that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.
"A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.
"Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she said, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.
She said that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.
However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), said she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.
She said that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages."
The proposals are currently being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.
They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.
IG Metall calls warning strike for Monday
The powerful IG Metall union said on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.
Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding company Meyer Werft and wind energy company
Siemens Gamesa.
The union said that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.
It says that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% wage increase.
So far, employers have offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.
Welcome back to our coverage
The DW newsroom says "Willkommen!" once more to all its readers as we resume our reporting on all things German.
Some good news is on the agenda: The Rhine River, which we can see from the window of our Bonn office, has recovered after a long period with little rainfall, meaning that the barges plying the waterway can load up properly again.
In other stories, the German president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is setting off on a trip to Africa, during which he is set to visit three countries with a businesss delegation in tow.
And Germany's powerful IG Metall union has said it is launching another 24-hour strike on Monday amid an escalating pay dispute.
Read on to find out more about what is happening in Germany on Sunday, November 22.
We're pausing our coverage
We're pausing our Germany news blog for now. Come back for more on Sunday!
Nmecha shows off new goal celebration after controversy
A new goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.
After scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.
Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.
However, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.
This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.
Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength."
The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.
Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke said he asked the player not to do the celebration again.
Dortmund overtakes Bayern in Bundesliga standings
Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.
Meanwhile, Bayern Munich was held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, and striker Harry Kane suffered a serious ankle injury. The Ballon d'Or winner is set to miss several months after undergoing ankle surgery earlier on Saturday.

Seven sus
items.text:
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI’s 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.
Fausto Isidro “Chapo Isidro” Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico’s defence secretariat said.
Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added.
Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of “flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs” by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.
Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.
Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.
Using US intelligence on his whereabouts, Mexican special forces descended on his location using “stealth and surprise”, establishing a perimeter to prevent him from escaping and reinforcements arriving, Mexico’s defence secretariat said.
However, they “came under attack from gunfire and explosives” before entering the property and arresting Meza Flores, the secretariat continued.
Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave. Others appear to show people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds.
Eight people in total were arrested, including Meza Flores’ second-in-command, who is also his cousin, and his brother-in-law, who is the group’s financial operator, the secretariat added.
Meza Flores, his cousin, and his brother-in-law were flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the defence secretariat said. The other five remained in the state of Sinaloa.
Authorities also said they had seized multiple weapons during the operation, including a grenade launcher, as well as drugs and cash.
The US Consulate General in the city of Hermosillo said it was “monitoring reports of ongoing security operations, armed clashes, road blockades, and vehicle fires that occurred overnight in Ahome, Guamúchil, Guasave, and Navolato” following the arrest of Meza-Flores.
It advised US citizens to remain alert for potential violence in the area and for residents to remain sheltered in place.
When Meza Flores was added to the FBI’s most-wanted list in 2025, he was accused of “heinous crimes” including kidnapping, extortion and torture.
Then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had also unleashed a “scourge of illicit drugs” into the US via its southern border with Mexico.
He was initially charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 before being charged again in 2019.
The 44-year-old is alleged to have conspired to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019.
Meza Flores was originally a high-ranking member of the Beltrán Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to establish his own cartel by 2013.
His organisation has also engaged in what US officials described as an “extremely violent turf war” with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.
Meza Flores was added to the FBI’s most-wanted list after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills they seized in 2024.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on the country’s cartels in a bid to resist US intervention on Mexican soil. Mexico has welcomed closer collaboration but resisted US boots on the ground.
Trump made stemming the flow of drugs into the US across its southern border one of his key election pledges.

items.title: Highly lucrative: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba
items.summary:
British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.
Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba
items.text:
British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.
Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.
In the 1840s, Cuba was the most important foreign source of copper ore for the UK. Copper was critical to Manchester’s cotton industry, railways and telegraphy.
Previous research has revealed that dozens of financiers involved in the founding in 1694 of the Bank of England invested in enslavement.
Now, Evans’s research reveals that ties between key figures in the UK’s financial system and enslavement of African peoples continued even after the government outlawed it.
Britain abolished its trade in enslaved people in 1807 and passed legislation abolishing slavery in most of its empire in 1833.
However, as Britain’s Slavery Abolition Act was coming into force, “City of London figures” were developing mining of El Cobre’s copper ore deposits, an operation which depended on enslavement in Spanish-controlled Cuba.
Key players in the highly lucrative operation included the Bank of England directors Charles Pascoe Grenfell (1790-1867) and William Thompson (1792-1854), acting in a private capacity.
Enslaved copper miners at El Cobre were likely to have been trafficked to Cuba by illegal voyages from the Bight of Biafra, in modern-day Nigeria, as Evans details in his book, Slavery’s Long Goodbye – Capitalism, Nationalism and Christianity in the Age of British Emancipation.
The death rate at El Cobre means it is likely that thousands of Africans were exploited there. Their life stories remain largely undocumented. At the time, slavery was legal in Cuba but the importation of enslaved people was not.
As a partner in the Cobre mining and export company, Grenfell was a driving force in enslaved miners’ exploitation.
Cobre was “likely to be the largest slave enterprise in the western hemisphere” by the 1840s, Evans said. Investors who held Cobre shares from the outset received £102 in dividends for every £40 share between 1836 and 1865.
Grenfell was also a partner in a Swansea-based smelter Pascoe, Grenfell & Sons, which bought imports from the mine, in an era when the Welsh port was the centre of the global copper trade.
Meanwhile, Thompson, a former lord mayor of London, exploited enslaved miners through the ore export firm he directed, the Royal Santiago Company.
The UK is facing increased pressure to make a formal apology to Caribbean and African nations for Britain’s centuries-long perpetuation of transatlantic chattel slavery. Commonwealth leaders say “structured dialogue” with the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, will begin in the next year.
While the Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has claimed Britain has nothing to apologise for, scholarship – dating back to the Trinidadian statesman Eric Williams’s 1944 book, Capitalism and Slavery – reveals the global impact of the colonialism and chattel enslavement that was integral to British capitalism’s success.
Evans, a former professor at the University of South Wales, said: “As Britain ostentatiously winds down its own slave system in the 1830s, British capital is boosting slavery elsewhere in the western hemisphere.
“The illegal trade, involving French and Spanish merchants, was flourishing and substantial. There were British (anti-slavery) patrols off the coast of Cuba, but they’re relatively few in number and intercept only a very small proportion of slave ships.”
Conditions at El Cobre were “extremely brutal”, with daily violence and torture. “Slave catchers” were employed to snatch miners who tried to escape to the mountains.
In 1817, under British pressure, Spanish authorities signed a treaty that banned trafficking enslaved Africans to Cuba. But as Cuba’s sugar and coffee plantations relied on enslaved African workers, local colonial authorities ignored it, with 25,000 captives arriving in 1859 alone.
In 1843, pressure from the British and Foreign Anti-Slavery Society prompted legislation intended to prohibit British subjects from owning enslaved people in other jurisdictions, after undercover investigations exposed British mining companies’ activities in Brazil and Cuba, including at El Cobre.
But after lobbying by mining interests, parliament diluted the legislation, allowing companies to retain enslaved workers as their “property” and hire others. The concessions prompted abolitionists to withdraw their support for the law, which failed to end the exploitation.
Neither Grenfell nor Thompson appears to have faced legal penalties for their involvement. Grenfell became the Liberal MP for Preston in the late 1840s, later boasting that his father had been an abolitionist. Grenfell remained a B of E director until 1864.
Enslavement at El Cobre finally ended after Cuban revolutionaries captured the town from Spanish forces in November 1868. The rebel commander proclaimed the miners’ emancipation on New Year’s Eve, and formerly enslaved workers later joined Cuba’s liberation army.
Evans’s book explores Britain’s overlapping histories of slavery, capitalism and missionary Christianity through the lives of Grenfell and two of his cousins.
Evans added: “The British in the early 19th century had started to understand slavery as a national sin.
“In the classical age of abolition, you could do things like abstain from eating sugar from the West Indies.
“But with copper, you can’t do that because it’s embodied in the industrial world, and, in the age of joint-stock capitalism, you have many British people who invest in mining companies who genuinely didn’t know these companies were using enslaved workers.
“Slavery was rendered invisible by the complexity of industrial society. But British engagement with slavery continued long after Emancipation. It involved the mer

items.title: Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return
items.summary: There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. items.text:
There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight.
Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.
Facing a Birmingham side who arrived top of the table and with firmly held Premier League ambitions, Stoke dominated for an hour, the hitherto goal-shy George Hirst earning a well-deserved lead to send a bumper crowd into raptures. The hand-wringing that then followed Luca Bombino’s sending-off with half an hour remaining made the victory that followed all the sweeter. The 10 men of Stoke were superb. It was no surprise that it took considerable time to convince those in the stands to depart for home after the final whistle.
You see, it is not just that Stoke are second in the table, kept off top spot by goal difference. It is not even that they are undoubtedly the Championship’s form side, with just one defeat in their past 13 games. It is the whole feeling around the place; the resilience Robins has developed, and the belief that they can take on the big guns and beat them.
“We are a work in progress, but today was that step in quality against different opponents. A step up in class,” said Robins. “I thought we were really, really good. The intensity, bravery and the intent that we showed was everything that we asked for.
“And, on the back of that, you’ve got the support that are absolutely right behind us. They trust the players. That is a really good feeling. It’s a great feeling for the players. It’s a heady mix, really.”
Eight years have passed since Stoke were last in the top flight; eight years spent as the Championship equivalent of a sea sponge, doing the bare minimum to survive and letting defeats wash over them while remaining resolutely attached to the rocks of the bottom half of the table. During that time they have ended every campaign no higher than 14th and no lower than 18th. Now, something altogether different is afoot. And this may well be the win that convinces supporters to trust their upbeat instincts.
There was an unavoidable fact heading into Saturday’s game. Stoke’s four defeats this season had all come when tasked with opponents fighting at the top end of the table in Swansea, Southampton, Wolves and Middlesbrough. They had shown themselves capable against much of the division, but a failure to deliver against another Championship heavyweight would have raised legitimate questions about their realistic aspirations.
The three August defeats at the start of the campaign preceded the departure of their best player, Sorba Thomas. His replacement, Jack McGlynn, has been an inspired signing. That this victory came without the talismanic figure of Ethan Galbraith, who was absent through illness, is considerable.
As well as switching to a three-man defence following those season-opening losses, a key factor in their upturn has been the restoration of a touch of old-school Stoke; a physicality that was frequently evident on a cold Saturday afternoon.
Bobby Madley, the referee, did not always take kindly to such an approach – to the indignation of the home crowd, who frequently made their feelings clear – but there was no complaint over Bombino’s sending-off for a second yellow after a rash challenge that left him head in hands before the card had even been shown. Tears followed on his slow trudge towards the tunnel, but he need not have worried, with Birmingham barely threatening thereafter.
Given just five points separate the top eight in the Championship table, it would come as no great shock to see Stoke drop off at some point. They do not have the financial benefit of recent Premier League parachute payments or big-spending owners, they are not prolific goalscorers, and a look at their expected goals and expected points tallies shows them firmly in the bottom half of the table. But they are finding ways to win and if McGlynn has a habit of scoring from unexpectedly long distances, perhaps it is because he is good at it.
Before this weekend, Robins had revealed that a top-eight finish was the pre-season target. “You aim for the stars and hopefully you land trying to grab hold of one,” he had said, rather poetically.
If promotion is a “P” they dare not yet speak of, another one – playoffs – is becoming an increasingly realistic proposition. No more sticking to a rock. Swim free and prosper.

items.text:
César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.
It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.
“I get up, take them to school, go to the gym. I do pilates some days. I walk the dogs, play golf, then it’s after-school activities. I read, try to learn new things. I haven’t yet thought: ‘I’m bored,’” Azpilicueta says, although you wonder how long that will last. “Over the last 12 months I could see it. The summer before I already ‘hit the post’ with retirement. It’s natural: a day comes … if only I could play for ever but it is what it is and you have to keep evolving. I’m enjoying it.”
Don’t get the wrong idea. “In terms of controlling your time, playing every three days, always waiting on the next message: ‘Meet at …,’ it’s a release. But it’s not a liberation because you’re delighted to pull your boots on. An important part of your life ends; you kick a ball almost from the moment you walk, live your passion. Even last season – when there were days everything hurt, when you think: ‘How can I get injured like that?’ – I would make demands of myself, my teammates. I always liked that.
“I never thought I’d be a professional. I couldn’t tell you the moment I thought: ‘I’m a footballer,’” Azpilicueta continues, but he can tell you the score on his debut, for Osasuna in 2007. “One-nil win, Getafe.” Celta de Vigo were the last opponents: a 1-0 loss in May for Sevilla. Between those, more than 800 matches, 508 for Chelsea. Only five players have played more for Chelsea; no foreigner has.
“I don’t think anyone who saw me back then could explain how I played 11 years at Chelsea … and nor could I,” Azpilicueta says, and there’s that laugh again.
It’s a long time since he stood before his new teammates and sang an Estopa track. He arrived in London with a labrador and a sausage dog; he left a legend and the captain, with three kids and every trophy, a European and world champion.
Asked to define his career in a word, Azpilicueta goes for: constancia. Perseverance, consistency, commitment. He talks about the cruciate tear with Marseille aged 19 as a lesson, something that “changed my perspective and made me value discipline, preparation … Out of something negative I grew.” About always adapting, always overcoming, becoming what managers need you to be. There’s a laugh at the little lies – of course I’ve played on the left, boss – and the hours spent alone practising, convincing coaches or teammates to stay behind with him and go over it again and again.
“I arrived at Chelsea late in the market [in 2012],” Azpilicueta says. “My representative said: ‘We’ve spoken to Michael Emenalo, the sporting director, and they’re signing younger players.’ Oscar, Eden Hazard, Victor Moses, Marko Marin, Paulo Ferreira. I was 22. Doubts? Pfff … Olympique needed the money. Chelsea had just won the Champions League and I …”
That laugh. “I hadn’t played for Spain. What did Emenalo see in me? It’s hard to work it out. Also, what you are and what you become is different. You think: ‘What’s it going to be like?’ Another country, another pace, but Juan Mata was there, Fernando Torres, Oriol [Romeu]. Doctor [Paco] Biosca, Ivan the physio. Petr Cech spoke Spanish. Hazard and I spoke French together. I could [communicate] with the Brazilians. But it wasn’t just them. I integrated fast, tried to speak English.
“Not long after arriving there was this audience with fans. Fernando, Juan, Oriol and I. A Q&A. One said: ‘Look, your name is very difficult. Can we just call you Dave?’ Juan translated. I said: ‘Yeah, sure,’ thinking that they meant for the evening. And it stuck. Going down the street: ‘Hey, Dave!’ There was the occasional ‘Dave’ in the dressing room but mostly it was fans. I felt the affection.
“You go with an open mind and bit by bit carve yourself a place. Every time a new coach comes you think: ‘Now what? Will I fit?’ I started as a winger in Pamplona. At Chelsea I played right-back, left-back, a line of three which I hadn’t played in my life … lots of systems, lots of coaches.”
Twelve coaches, in fact. Azpilicueta played under all of them. ““You arrive at a historic club like Chelsea and just try to stay as long as you can. That machine makes demands of you every three days. What I really noticed was a hunger to win: either you have that culture or … forget it. At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe. You see teammates come and go. The reality is the reality. On the pitch, you have to do it. It’s hard? Yes. But you can’t be sunk by a bad game. If you win: very good, done, next. If you can’t perform, you’re out … You have to manage that pressure.
“I’ve had plenty of unpleasant days. I remember a 6-0 loss Manchester City.” So then what? “For me, the first thing would be watch the video. Look at the data. But know that’s not everything. Sleep, get up, turn it round. Get into to training first. And it’s not just about you; some days it’s about lifting up teammat

items.title: 'Completely unacceptable! - Vasseur slams Leclerc for Hamilton collision
items.summary:
Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur blames Charles Leclerc for 'unacceptable' collision with Lewis Hamilton in Las Vegas GP
The Ferrari team-mates clashed on track once again, just weeks after their costly collision in Mexico City derailed the team’s race; Charles Leclerc punished by stewards and blamed b
items.text:
Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur blames Charles Leclerc for 'unacceptable' collision with Lewis Hamilton in Las Vegas GP
The Ferrari team-mates clashed on track once again, just weeks after their costly collision in Mexico City derailed the team’s race; Charles Leclerc punished by stewards and blamed by team boss Frederic Vasseur after spinning Lewis Hamilton in battle over sixth place
Sunday 22 November 2026 08:01, UK
Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur blamed Charles Leclerc for a "completely unacceptable" collision with team-mate Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
The Ferrari drivers made contact when battling over sixth place with 12 laps remaining in a breathless, frenzied race in which the team were attempting to recover from a poor qualifying when both drivers were knocked out in Q2.
Hamilton was spun around in the Turn Seven-collision, dropping to 10th in the order. Leclerc was found to be at fault by race stewards, who imposed a 10-second penalty on him.
- Las Vegas GP race result

That was applied to Leclerc's final race time and dropped him to 10th place in the final classification, with Hamilton ending up seventh.
Two weeks after speaking to both drivers to remind them of their responsibilities to the team after a squabble on track in Mexico had cost them a likely win, Vasseur was left unimpressed. He also revealed they had asked Leclerc not to overtake Hamilton given they did not want the drivers fighting amongst themselves and leave them vulnerable to slip-streaming rivals.
"Clearly, it's unacceptable," Vasseur told Sky Italy.
"A little bit the same message as Mexico because you have to think about the team, about the people working in Maranello. About all the stakeholders, the sponsors and so on.
"We told Charles not to overtake, because in a race like this, you have to focus on your own race rather than risk being overtaken by others. Charles clearly made a mistake, and it has cost the team dearly. What happened today [Sunday] is completely unacceptable.
"Honestly, I am more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico.
"We had a chat all together in Brazil. Today we passed the message to think about the team when they were racing together and the outcome is this one. It's mega frustrating for all of us."
'I'm penalised so it has to be my mistake' - Leclerc frustrated but accepts decision
In their report confirming the decision to penalise Leclerc, the stewards said the Monegasque had started his move on Hamilton from "a considerable distance behind" in the sister Ferrari, Hamilton's car, and had "not earned the right to the corner" by the apex.
They therefore found him to be "wholly to blame".
On Leclerc's cool-down lap back to the pits at the end of the race, Vasseur told him on Ferrari team radio: "Charles, I want to see you just after the race, before everything"
While stopping short of any apology in his post-race interview, instead saying he was "embarrassed for the team", a visibly-frustrated Leclerc said he accepted the stewards' decision.
"I have been penalised so, as a result, I guess the majority and the stewards thought that it was my mistake. I'll accept that," Leclerc told Sky Sports F1.
"I'm not going to say much more. At the end of the day, I'm penalised so it has to be my mistake."
Asked if Ferrari now needed to impose stricter rules, Leclerc said: "Well, I just feel quite embarrassed for the team in general. We'll review."

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a crazy, slipstreaming Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years, whi
items.text:
Max Verstappen wins F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix for third time in four years
Red Bull’s Verstappen dug deep to fend off Antonelli and Russell in a race that saw a jaw-dropping 35 lead changes.
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a crazy, slipstreaming Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years, while Mercedes rival George Russell hit the barriers late on and finished ninth.
In a race featuring 35 lead changes over 50 laps, with drivers running nose-to-tail under the floodlights and track advantage swinging back and forth like a yo-yo, McLaren’s 2025 champion Lando Norris and teammate Oscar Piastri finished second and third behind the pole-sitter on Saturday.
Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided again in a race in which both collected 10-second penalties for separate incidents and finished seventh and 10th, respectively.
“That was crazy. Really, really surreal and something I’ve never seen before in Formula One myself,” said Verstappen, who beat Norris by 0.639 seconds.
“It was a crazy amount of fighting, and the slipstream was so big that it was just impossible to drive off and it was just crazy how many people were just following.”
Mercedes have already won both titles, with 20-year-old Italian Kimi Antonelli this month becoming the youngest ever Formula One world champion, while Verstappen and Russell started the weekend scrapping to end the season as overall runner-up.
Verstappen’s fourth win in six races sent him 37 points clear of Ferrari’s Hamilton, with Russell, who started on the front row, dropping to fourth overall and level with Norris.
Antonelli was fourth, with Alpine’s Pierre Gasly fifth and teammate Franco Colapinto sixth. Carlos Sainz was eighth for Williams in the Spaniard’s 250th race.
“I think that must have been the most chaotic race ever in the history of Formula One,” said Norris.
“I didn’t know what was happening half the time. I didn’t know if I was going to have the best race and have a chance to win or end up last. It had everything this race.”
Piastri, who started 17th, could only agree.
“They say Las Vegas is the entertainment capital of the world and that was pretty entertaining to be a part of,” said the Australian.
“It was pretty random. You would pass someone on one straight super easy, then the next straight you would struggle and then with someone else it would be different strengths and weaknesses.”

items.title: Murkomen promises corruption-free police recruitment ahead of December 10 exercise
items.summary:
NAIROBI,Kenya Nov 22 – Interior and National Administration Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has assured Kenyans that the forthcoming police recruitment exercise will be free, fair and transparent, warning against corruption and interference in the selection process.
The National Police Service
items.text:
NAIROBI,Kenya Nov 22 – Interior and National Administration Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has assured Kenyans that the forthcoming police recruitment exercise will be free, fair and transparent, warning against corruption and interference in the selection process.
The National Police Service (NPS) has scheduled the nationwide recruitment of police constables for Thursday, December 10, 2026, with the exercise set to run from 8am to 5pm at 423 designated centres across all 47 counties.
All applicants will be required to report to their respective recruitment centres by 8am for the exercise.
Murkomen said the Government would open the recruitment process to public scrutiny by allowing independent observers at recruitment centres to ensure that only qualified candidates are enlisted into the National Police Service.
“The recruitment will be conducted properly, without corruption. We invite observers to the recruitment centres to ensure that those who emerge the best are the ones recruited,” he said.
The CS said the exercise would be guided by merit, insisting that qualified candidates would be given equal opportunities to join the police service.
According to the recruitment advertisement, applicants must be Kenyan citizens aged between 18 and 28 years, hold valid national identity cards and have attained a minimum KCSE grade of D+, with at least a D+ in either English or Kiswahili.
Candidates must also meet the prescribed physical and medical fitness requirements, including minimum height requirements of five feet eight inches for men and five feet three inches for women.
Applicants will be required to present their national identity cards, birth certificates, academic certificates and testimonials during the exercise.
The police service has warned candidates against paying bribes or engaging individuals promising to secure them positions, insisting that the recruitment is free and that corruption or attempts to influence the process constitute criminal offences.
Murkomen spoke at Amaya Plesian Grounds in Tiaty, Baringo County, during a security assessment visit, where he also presided over the Amaya Youth Empowerment Initiative.
He said the Government was committed to strengthening security operations in the region, announcing plans to intensify efforts to tackle banditry in the troubled Kerio Valley region.
“Those saying that they don’t want security officers, we want to tell them that our operations will be increased sixfold to liberate the Kerio Valley region from banditry,” he said.
The CS directed security officers involved in the operations to adopt intelligence-led approaches, targeting identified criminals and their accomplices while protecting innocent residents.
He said the Government would not relent in restoring security in areas affected by banditry, adding that operations would be intensified in the remaining troubled areas.
Murkomen was accompanied by Baringo Senator Vincent Chemitei, Tiaty MP William Kamket, Baringo County Commissioner Ronald Enyakasi and several Members of County Assembly, among other leaders.

items.text:
Indonesia factory fire kills three, 36 missing
Rescue crews continue looking for missing workers in destroyed three-story facility near Jakarta.
A fire at a sweets factory in Indonesia has killed at least three people and 36 others are missing.
At least 15 people were rescued from the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province, which borders the capital Jakarta, including four taken to hospital, said the National Search and Rescue Agency in a statement on Sunday.
“The fire is still burning in several locations and firefighting teams are continuing extinguishing and cooling operations,” rescue official Rizky Dwianto told The Associated Press news agency.
Firefighters from Serang district and Banten province were battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the fire began, Dwianto said.
Rescue workers along with fire department personnel and the Indonesian Red Cross searched different sections of the factory, focusing on areas where victims might be trapped, he added.
Around 60 people were in the factory when the fire started. Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters.
The factory produces milk-based snacks and sweets, known as Milkita.
Photos and videos circulating online captured black flames and thick smoke coming from the three-storey building. Footage from inside appeared to show the fire caused extensive damage, with equipment blackened and destroyed.
Local broadcasters and social media accounts shared footage of families gathering outside the factory.
The disaster agency said the cause of the fire was under investigation.
Indonesia has suffered a number of deadly fires in recent years. A fire in an office building in Jakarta killed at least 22 people last December. An explosion at an Indonesian nickel-processing plant killed at least 13 people in 2023.

items.text:
Wembanyama scores 50 points, bags 19 rebounds in Spurs’ 14th win of season
Wembanyama became only the third NBA player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game.
Victor Wembanyama has scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds to power San Antonio to a 114-91 victory over New Orleans as the Spurs matched the National Basketball Association’s best record at 14-3.
The 22-year-old, 7-foot-4-inch (2.24m) Frenchman made 20 of 29 shots from the floor, 5 of 11 from three-point range, and added five blocked shots, four steals and an assist in 32 minutes on the court on Saturday.
San Antonio won for the 14th time in 15 games, and Wembanyama became only the third NBA player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game.
“It is very special, but unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding,” Wembanyama said.
Wembanyama was just shy of his career-high score of 52 points, set in a victory over Dallas on November 4.
“Wemby” scored 17 points in the first quarter as the Spurs jumped to a 32-29 lead over the visiting Pelicans and had 32 points and 13 rebounds at half-time with San Antonio ahead 61-45.
“I thought he started the game off aggressive, and I thought he was trying to play with a lot of force offensively, specifically, just in terms of taking up real estate, trying to get to the rim,” Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said.
“I thought he did a really good job of playing with force.”
Johnson did not relish taking Wemby to the bench but wanted to avoid any chance of an injury in a game well in hand.
“Was it tough to pull him out after he got 50? No, I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did,” Johnson said. “That would have been hard to take him out that close to 50.”
The Spurs levelled with the Los Angeles Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the best record in the league, the Sixers having matched the mark earlier in a 132-129 victory over Milwaukee.
Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a fifth consecutive victory despite Tyler Herro’s career-high 50 points for the Bucks.
Embiid delivered 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds and nine assists for the host Sixers as they dropped the league-worst Bucks to 1-16, stretching Milwaukee’s losing skid to 13 games.
Herro added 11 rebounds and seven assists, but he missed a chance to send the game into overtime.
He sank a three-point shot at the finish, but officials ruled after consulting video replay that the shot left his hand after the final buzzer.
Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player LeBron James scored 21 points, grabbed six rebounds, recorded three steals and provided six assists for the 76ers.
“For us to be a super complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious,” James said. “It’s key for our other guys as well to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident.”
Anfernee Simons added 18 points off the Philadelphia bench while Tyrese Maxey added 17 and VJ Edgecombe scored 16 as the 76ers withstood a late Bucks rally.
“Soon we’re going to have to put together a 48-minute game,” Maxey said.
Bridges buzzer winner
At Madison Square Garden, Mikal Bridges sank a three-pointer at the final buzzer to give the reigning champions New York Knicks a 97-96 victory over Portland.
The Trail Blazers rallied from a 26-point deficit to seize a 96-94 lead on two free throws by Deni Avdija with 3.2 seconds remaining.
The Knicks tried to inbound the ball to star Jalen Brunson for the last shot but went to Bridges when Brunson was covered.
“They played harder than us in that second half,” Bridges said. “That’s on us, but we just finished the game. It goes 48 minutes, and we just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning.”
The Knicks, without injured starters OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns, improved to 10-6 with their fourth consecutive victory while Portland fell to 10-6.
Brunson led New York with 30 points, 19 of them in the first quarter, while Landry Shamet added 20 and Bridges had 12 points.
In other games, Jaden McDaniels scored 25 points to lead Minnesota’s 104-95 home win over Memphis, while Kyrie Irving had 25 points and Cooper Flagg added 22 in a 110-100 Dallas home win over the Los Angeles Clippers.

The joint operation by the National Police Service (NPS) and the National Transport and Safety Authority (NTSA) has
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 22 – Several vehicles have been detained in a nationwide traffic crackdown targeting motorists and transport operators accused of violating road safety regulations.
The joint operation by the National Police Service (NPS) and the National Transport and Safety Authority (NTSA) has targeted public service vehicles (PSVs), commercial trucks, boda boda riders and tuk-tuk operators in multiple counties.
The enforcement exercises have been conducted along major highways, including at Diani in Kwale County, Maungu in Taita Taveta and Salama in Makueni, where officers intercepted vehicles over various traffic violations.
The crackdown is part of intensified efforts to remove unroadworthy vehicles from Kenyan roads, enforce compliance and prevent accidents as authorities combine enforcement with public road safety awareness campaigns.
In the Coast region, traffic officers also held sensitisation exercises with transport operators, commuters and members of the public, highlighting the importance of adhering to traffic regulations.
In Mombasa, Central Traffic Base officers joined the Mvita Deputy County Commissioner, NTSA officials, county enforcement officers and private sector partners at Tononoka Grounds for a road safety engagement organised by the 001 Tuk Tuk Sacco.
The event also marked the launch of Class A3 driving licence endorsement training for 50 tuk-tuk riders, aimed at improving their skills and compliance with licensing requirements.
Meanwhile, Likoni Traffic Base officers conducted a separate sensitisation exercise targeting boda boda riders in the Jamsa area.
In Tana River County, Hola Traffic Base officers partnered with the Kenya Rural Roads Authority (KeRRA) to educate residents and transport operators on road safety.
The campaign focused on protecting road furniture, preventing vandalism, obeying traffic signs and ensuring passengers are picked up and dropped off only at designated stages.
In the Central region, traffic bases in Kiambu, Sagana and Maragua also conducted sensitisation campaigns targeting boda boda operators.
At Ngoliba in Kiambu County, officers engaged National Youth Service (NYS) students, urging them to observe discipline on the roads, avoid boarding overloaded vehicles and report reckless drivers and conductors.
The National Police Service said joint enforcement operations and public sensitisation campaigns would continue daily across the country.
It urged all road users, including motorists, pedestrians and public transport operators, to observe traffic regulations, warning that compliance was critical in reducing road accidents and protecting lives.

Masked US immigration officers have detained two people on an airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers boarded a flight to Los Angeles, prompting criticism from Washington state Governor Bob Ferguson and concer
items.text:
US: ICE arrests 2 at Seattle airport in 'chilling' scenes — governor
November 22, 2026
Masked US immigration officers have detained two people on an airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers boarded a flight to Los Angeles, prompting criticism from Washington state Governor Bob Ferguson and concerns from Alaska Airlines.
The arrests took place at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport around 8 a.m. local time (1600 UTC) on Saturday. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said the operation targeted Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who had overstayed his visa.
Agents also arrested Sofia Hernandez Mejia, who they alleged threw hot coffee at the ICE officers during the confrontation. ICE said she had also overstayed her visa and would face a charge of assaulting a federal officer.
Videos of the incident circulated on social media, showing officers struggling with a person on the ground as passengers look on. One woman could be heard shouting that her daughter was being taken away and that she had a work permit.
Washington governor slams 'out of control' ICE
Governor Ferguson, a Democrat, described the footage as "horrific" and "chilling", accusing ICE of being "completely and totally out of control."
He urged Alaska Airlines to ask federal immigration authorities to leave the state's airports and said he would make the same appeal to other airlines operating at Seattle-Tacoma.
Alaska Airlines said it had received no advance notice of the enforcement operation and was working to understand the circumstances.
The airline also expressed concern over the incident, which it said had been distressing for passengers and employees.
The operation drew criticism from April Sims, president of the Washington State Labor Council, AFL-CIO, who said it had caused fear and disruption during one of the busiest travel periods of the year.
The flight was delayed, with Alaska Airlines saying many passengers were transferred to other flights. The original service eventually departed at 11 a.m. local time.

India: Nepal PM Balendra Shah heads to Delhi for first bilateral visit
Published November 21, 2026last updated November 22, 2026
What you need to know
- Nepal's Balendra Shah is set to arrive in India for his first foreign bilateral visit since becoming prime minister earlier this year
- India's men post a record 720 runs at stumps on day 4 of test against New Zealand

- Over 200 people are hospitalized after consuming toxic liquor in Manipur state
Here is a roundup of the main headlines from India on Saturday, November 21 and Sunday, November 22:
Nepal PM Balendra Shah set to arrive in Delhi
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah is set to arrive in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day visit, his first bilateral trip since taking office in March.
The 36-year-old former rapper will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. He will also meet Foreign Minister S Jaishankar and briefly visit President Droupadi Murmu.
Reconstruction after August's devastating floods is expected to dominate the talks. The disaster left some 1,500 dead and more than 5,200 missing, with roads, bridges, power plants, farms and homes destroyed.
Nepal estimates rebuilding will cost $4.78 billion.
Nepal is also pressing for an extra route for commercial flights to Bhairahawa and Pokhara.
"India is a major and important partner for Nepal," Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai told reporters, saying the leaders would discuss trade, transit, investment, energy, connectivity and infrastructure.
New Delhi said the visit "reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal," AFP reported. Local media reported that talks may also touch upon unresolved border disputes.
India is Nepal's largest trading partner, accounting for more than 60% of its imports, worth $8.6 billion, versus China's 13%, according to World Bank figures. India and China regularly compete for influence in Nepal.
Shah will be accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal.
Welcome back to our coverage
Hello! We are back with the latest news from India this Sunday.
Nepal's rapper-turned-prime minister Balendra Shah is in New Delhi for his first bilateral foreign visit since taking office.
Meanwhile, India has posted a record total of 720-9 on the fourth day of the first cricket test against New Zealand.
For this and more, follow our blog.
We're pausing the blog
We're logging off today, but we will be back tomorrow with the latest from across India.
Stay tuned for more!
Youth Congress protests at Meta offices over restricted Instagram accounts
Workers of the Indian Youth Congress (IYC), the youth wing of the opposition Indian National Congress, protested at US tech giant Meta's offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram on Friday, demanding that the group's leaders' Instagram accounts be restored.
In Hyderabad, protesters entered the building, smashed plants and clashed with police, according to footage the IYC released. Meta declined to comment.
The IYC said Instagram withheld the accounts of its president and in-charge on November 19 "on BJP orders," referring to the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, and restored both shortly after the protests.
Manu Jain, who runs the group's social media, told Reuters thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted.
BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said: "Congress is a party of goons! Goons of Indian Youth Congress are not only vandalized and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad, & also are flaunting it on social media!"
Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav warned foreign companies against getting involved in Indian politics.
The Indian government says it orders takedowns only for content that breaches local laws or threatens public safety or national security. In February, it cut the deadline for removing unlawful content from 36 hours to three.
Meta restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in the previous six months, saying most were cases where local law required it to restrict content proactively.
Earlier this month, Brazil’s top electoral court fined Meta's Facebook $1.3 million for failing to comply with judicial orders during the country's presidential election runoff campaign. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's team accused the company of political bias.
Rahul, Gill puts India 118 ahead of New Zealand on day three in Wellington
India closed day three of the first Test against New Zealand on 486-4, a lead of 118 runs. KL Rahul made 136, Shubman Gill 98 and Rishabh Pant was unbeaten on 55 as every one of India's top five passed 50.
Rahul reached his 13th Test hundred off 207 balls, batting for more than eight hours and sharing stands of 165 with Devdutt Padikkal (80) and 91 with Gill. It completed a set of Test centuries in every major Test-playing nation outside the subcontinent for the Indian wicketkeeper-batsman.
"It feels really awesome, actually, to be able to achieve something like that," Rahul said.
He survived an LBW appeal on 5 that was given not out and New Zealand chose not to review. "Those 15 seconds were probably the slowest 15 seconds of my life," he said of the review process.
Gill and Pant added 100 in the final session before Gill was bowled by Jacob Duffy just before stumps. Duffy finished with 1-180 from 29 overs, the fourth most expensive figures in New Zealand's Test history, AFP said.
The pitch, green on day one, flattened out. "We expected a lot of grass on the wicket, we expected a lot of movement and it has probably not panned out that way," Padikkal said.
New Zealand were all out for 368 in their first innings.
The two-match series ends next week in Christchurch.

items.text:
Why Arsenal are behind in race for Champions League spots
- Published
Before the 2026-27 season began, Arsenal technical director Jodie Taylor declared: "I'll flat out say it: we want to win the league and want to take that next step."
After finishing second last season, it seemed like a logical statement to make.
However, after 10 games in this season's Women's Super League, they are sixth in the table, trailing leaders Chelsea by 13 points.
They are also nine points behind third-placed London City Lionesses, albeit with a game in hand, and facing stiff competition to qualify for the Champions League again next campaign.
BBC Sport looks at where things have gone wrong for the Gunners, who have not won the WSL since 2018-19.
Poor form at Emirates Stadium
Last term, Arsenal hosted all 11 of their league home games at Emirates Stadium for the first time, winning eight times and drawing on three occasions.
This season, Renee Slegers' side have drawn all five of their home games and will seek their first win at the sixth attempt when they host West Ham on Sunday (14:30 GMT), live on BBC Two.
Two of those draws came against promoted sides Crystal Palace and Birmingham City, where a combined 57 shots yielded just one goal.
Home fans are getting disgruntled and this has been reflected in attendances. Last season, the Gunners had an average attendance of 33,808, better than eight Premier League clubs.
So far this year their biggest crowd was against London City Lionesses last weekend, when 32,588 were in the stands.
Speaking on the Women's Football Weekly podcast, former England striker Ellen White said: "The Emirates seems [like] a bit of an issue for them at the moment - they just can't get that win there.
"A draw might feel like a loss for them because they are so far behind now in terms of the Champions League spots."
Former Gunners striker Vivianne Miedema, who did play at Emirates Stadium for Arsenal but joined Manchester City before the full switch was made, added: "Players always say that the crowd really, really helps you at Arsenal. The fans are amazing - it gives you that extra bit of energy.
"Obviously playing in the Emirates with all the fans should still give them that boost but it doesn't seem to be fully working for them this season so far."
Plenty of shots - but a lack of clinical edge
The Gunners have had 199 shots in 10 league matches but managed just 11 goals. That is just over one goal per game, and their conversion rate of 5.53% is the lowest of any club over the past six seasons.
Part of the problem could be an over-reliance on key goalscorer Alessia Russo.
She has alternated between the number nine and number 10 position during the season but thrives most when she is the focal point in the attack.
This season, the England striker has five league goals and provided two assists, with her form improving in recent weeks.
She was player of the match against Tottenham after scoring and providing an assist in a 2-1 win and similarly against Liverpool, when she scored twice to help Arsenal triumph by the same scoreline.
After Russo, only Lisa Baum (two), Georgia Stanway (two), Smilla Holmberg and Frida Maanum have scored in the league.
Injuries to attacking options Chloe Kelly, Selina Cerci and Stina Blackstenius have also proved costly, while key midfielder Mariona Caldentey is about halfway through an expected 10-week absence with a hamstring injury.
The result is that Arsenal and Brighton are the only teams in the league to have a goal difference of zero after 10 games.
Contrast that with title rivals Chelsea, who have scored 29 goals and have a goal difference of +24, while defending champions Manchester City have netted 27 times.
Slegers' future has been questioned
While Slegers will always be hailed for winning Arsenal's second Champions League title last year against Barcelona, questions have been asked about her future after another slow start to the season.
In three of their home league matches, Arsenal have fallen behind and dropped points. Last Sunday, they went ahead against London City but only held the lead for 98 seconds.
It was a big summer of change in north London with club stalwarts Katie McCabe and Beth Mead among those departing, and seven new signings arriving including Stanway, Cerci and Baum.
Also among the arrivals was Swiss midfielder Geraldine Reuteler, who helped her country reach the quarter-finals of Euro 2025 but has struggled for minutes since signing a four-year deal in the summer.
She has made just four appearances across all competitions, appearing for a total of just 66 minutes in the WSL.
The results have left Slegers vulnerable and a first home win of the season against West Ham would be a much-needed boost for a side that have fallen far short of the lofty targets they set back in September.

items.text:
Argentina midfielder Paredes collapses during TV interview
- Published
World Cup winning midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed while giving a post-match interview minutes after winning a trophy with Boca Juniors.
The former Paris St-Germain midfielder, 32, was suffering with the heat and humidity in Barranquilla, Colombia, where Boca won the Copa Sudamericana by beating Atletico Mineiro of Brazil 2-0.
He was replaced during the second half, then collapsed while being interviewed on television, with pictures showing a journalist trying to break his fall.
After some treatment Argentine Paredes was able to walk to the dressing room and joined in with his team's celebrations.
"Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just dizziness," he said on Instagram, external after the match.
Heat was a discussion before the game with forecasts predicting tempertures could reach 32C and humidity around 80%.
Boca manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena said he noticed the midfielder's difficulties during the second half.
"He felt dizzy towards the end of the first half," Arruabarrena said.
"He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second half you could see he was struggling."
Paredes started his career with Boca before moving to Europe in 2015.
The victory for Boca ended an 18-year international trophy drought for the Argentine side.
By securing their 19th international cup, Boca also became South America's most decorated club since 1960, overtaking domestic rivals Independiente who have 18.
