items.text:
Fossil fuel impasse pushes COP31 climate talks into second day of overtime
COP31 President Murat Kurum asks negotiators to consider a last-minute proposal in attempt to reach an agreement.
Turkish officials have asked negotiators at the COP31 climate summit to consider a last-minute proposal as talks stretched into a second day of overtime over the fossil fuels issue.
“We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary session on Saturday.
Kurum, who is also Turkiye’s environment minister, said the conference would reconvene later on Sunday morning to approve the deal.
The latest text was not immediately made public, and it was unclear if negotiators had received the wording overnight, which would give nations only a few hours to submit objections and changes.
An earlier draft had drawn strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels, the largest contributors to climate change.
Kurum said he believed concerns around fossil fuels had been addressed, as had those around helping developing countries finance their adaptations to climate change.
The new text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is leading the talks; Turkiye, which is hosting the meeting; and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.
Delegations had until 03:00 GMT on Sunday to raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 06:00 GMT to begin approving it.
The summit’s agreement is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which drives heatwaves, floods and other disasters.
An opening draft from Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.
Key issues that slowed down the agreement included how much effort countries should make to wean themselves off fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and gas.
Other issues included whether to encourage industrial carbon capture and storage of pollutants, as well as whether ramping up electricity should only be done with renewables, such as wind and solar, or also involve other sources like natural gas and coal.
To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut fossil fuel emissions.
The two-week talks in the Turkish city of Antalya were due to end on Friday.
In a letter sent on Saturday to this year’s cohosts, Turkiye and Australia, 100 civil society groups warned that they were “on course to preside over one of the most disappointing COPs” the UN has ever held.
The letter stated there were only hours left “to save this COP from becoming a low point of three decades of climate negotiations”.
In the lead-up to these talks, the United Nations said the world would likely blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.

items.title: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to standardize parts to lower costs
items.summary:

- The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for
items.text:
- Toyota, Nissan, and Honda will begin standardizing some vehicle parts in an effort to lower production costs, according to a report by Automotive News.
- The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses.
- Discussions are starting with Japan’s domestic suppliers, though international suppliers will be looped in soon.
Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.
In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.
For Sale Near You
See all results for used Toyota for sale near 97347
The first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.
The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.
“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”

After a brief stint as a detailer for a local dealership group in college, he knew he needed a more permanent way to drive all the new cars he couldn’t afford and decided to pursue a career in auto writing. By hounding his college professors at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, he was able to travel Wisconsin seeking out stories in the auto world before landing his dream job at Car and Driver. His new goal is to delay the inevitable demise of his 2010 Volkswagen Golf.

items.title: Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit
items.summary:
It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.

items.text:
It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.
Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute Olimpico from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.
The Spirit, heartbroken at the final whistle, have now lost three consecutive NWSL Championships.
“Obviously this one hates way worse than any of the other ones,” forward Trinity Rodman said afterward. “I don’t even think you have words in this moment — it is too fresh.”
DiBernardo’s goal was stunning, a driven, bent corner kick played to the far post that eluded Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver, her defenders and Current forward Haley Hopkins, potentially DiBernardo’s intended target. The Spirit’s players and fans alike pleaded with center referee Joshua Encarnación, suggesting he examine the play on VAR for obstruction, as MacIver had potentially been screened. The review never came.
Whether played directly on goal intentionally or otherwise, the effort will go down as one of the most memorable in NWSL Championship history. At 34, DiBernardo becomes the oldest player in league history to score in a final, and was later named the match’s MVP.
“I’ve been to the game a few times and haven’t won, but this one just felt a little lighter,” said DiBernardo, who gave birth to Charlie, her first child, in January and took time off before returning to the Current in March. “I think just having Charlie, it just brings a different perspective on life. I knew the game was big and it was a big moment, but just kinda having her, just spending the day with her, it just felt really special.”
The game’s early phases were forgettable save for one incident which would go on to affect the remainder of the match: a bruising, high-speed tackle on Rodman by Current defender Laney Rouse in the fifth minute. The challenge sent Rodman flying and appeared to injure her left elbow; the Spirit forward, nearing tears, spent much of the first half in visible pain and seemingly never fully recovered. Rouse was not cautioned for the challenge.
“[It helped set the tone] in the sense that it hurt really bad, yes,” Rodman said. “As a team, you always want to put the first hit in. You’re taught to do that. Credit to them. I wish I was the one who put her on the ground. They did a really good job at setting the tone and controlling the first half.”
It was far from the game’s only physical moment. Neither team managed to settle into any meaningful rhythm during an opening 45 that felt at times more like a title fight than a title match. Encarnación, involved in his first NWSL final, called a very tight match and the near-constant stoppages in play were the defining characteristic of a sometimes ugly opening phase. In many ways it was not entirely his fault: the message-sending start from KC and the Spirit’s subsequent response often compelled him to act. The 19 combined first-half fouls between both sides were the most in any half of any NWSL title match in league history.
“It felt like we couldn’t play more than two minutes without a whistle,” Rodman said. “We were fouling, they were true calls for sure — but I think you lose control of the game really quickly that way ... It definitely messed with our rhythm a little bit.”
Paradoxically, though, the match was won with speed. Deep into second-half stoppage time, the Current found their eventual match-winner on a breakaway. After doggedly winning back possession after a Spirit free kick late on, Kansas City forward Debinha streaked upfield from just beyond the center stripe, looking off a wide-open Temwa Chawinga and rounding MacIver who looked on hopelessly as the Brazilian slotted it home.
Moments later, Rodman – somehow still in the match after not only the early challenge but a later high-speed collision with Current goalkeeper Lorena – pulled one back for the Spirit. Falling away from goal 10 yards out, Rodman got her head on the end of a Tara Rudd cross, placing it perfectly over Lorena’s outstretched arms and into the far-side netting. The ensuing five minutes – the game ended in the 102nd – were chaotic but the Spirit couldn’t quite find the equalizer.
After a slow start, the Current were well-managed by former Major League Soccer and US national team member Chris Armas. Armas was widely considered a controversial selection at the time of his appointment but proceeded to lead the club to their first championship in his first season, doing so by beating Gotham FC and now the Spirit, two sides picked by many as potential league-winners.
“I think from the front to the back we made it a point that every person on this team defends and if somebody is going to make a mistake the other person is going to have their back,” Current defender Izzy Rodriguez said. “We try and turn every 1v1 situation into a 1v2 for us, and I think that showed up today. We were winning our duels and second balls and those are things that win games.”
For the Spirit, the loss is devastating. They become the first American professional club – men’s or women’s – to lose three consecutive finals since the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer, who did so in the mid 2000s. In their five Championship appearances, the Spirit have won just one time, in 2021.

items.text:
Eleven killed in burst of violence during Mexican cartel leader’s capture
Seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the operation to arrest Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.
The operation to capture Mexican cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in the country’s Sinaloa state has left at least 11 people dead.
Mexico’s Defence Ministry said on Saturday that seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers were killed in the overnight operation.
Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was captured on Friday and flown to Mexico City on Saturday after hours-long violence involving a firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen overnight, roadblocks and burning trucks in the city of Guasave.
Two other men were also captured and flown to Mexico City. The ministry identified them as German N, known as “Serafin”, the group’s alleged second-in-command, and Jose N, an alleged financial operator of the cartel. Both were also flown to Mexico City and handed over to prosecutors.
Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, climbed the ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later became the boss of his own group, the Meza-Flores transnational criminal organisation.
He was also a key ally to “Los Mayos”, a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which the United States designated as a “foreign terrorist organization” last year.
The US wanted Meza Flores for trafficking drugs to the country and offered a $5m reward for information leading to his arrest.
Residents terrified
The firefight in Guasave broke out about 7pm on Friday (02:00 GMT on Saturday), according to residents. Military helicopters and drones were soon flying overhead, with helicopters opening fire on key locations across the city.
Videos show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and businesses, and circling helicopters shooting at people below.
Because of the violence, the Mexican army and National Guard special forces were unable to extract Meza Flores from Guasave until 4am (11:00 GMT) on Saturday, said a federal official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to discuss the case.
While a tense calm has settled over Guasave since the operation, experts warned that picking off cartel bosses could set off more waves of violence in a region already caught up in a power struggle between warring factions.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has been under pressure from US President Donald Trump to crack down on cartels and has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors. Homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office.
The US Drug Enforcement Administration commended Mexican authorities, as did Washington’s ambassador to Mexico.
“Results like these don’t happen overnight. They are built on sustained cooperation and trust. This is what partners can accomplish together,” US Ambassador Ronald Johnson said in an X post.

Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial site on Saturday evening, as two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran reported shooting dow a US drone amid stalled efforts to end the war.

Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the Middle East conflict.
The Gulf kingdom has suffered several attacks this week, ending a weeks-long lull in the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.
"As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the interior ministry said on X, without specifying the location.
To display this content from X (Twitter), you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
Residents said they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain's east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said "during the operation, US military positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain were targeted with missile and drone strikes".
"Two radars belonging to the US Army's Patriot air defense systems... were struck," it said, adding that any violation of Iranian airspace will be met with "harsh and decisive response".
The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping line.
The US military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried about one-fifth of the world's oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.
Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks", without providing details.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: "The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally."
"Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state TV.
Iran's demands include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Iran says shot down drone
British maritime agency UKMTO said Saturday one tanker was struck by an "unknown projectile" while transiting Hormuz.
"There are no reported casualties at this time," it said, adding another tanker was hit in its engine room.
Iran's army later reported a ship was on fire after entering a "restricted zone" and hitting a mine in the strait.
The tanker had switched off its identification and navigation systems "in defiance of issued warnings and maritime transit regulations", it said in a statement carried by state TV.
Tehran has repeatedly reported ships catching fire in the strait in recent weeks, often claiming they struck mines.
But the US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.
US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
Iran said on Saturday it shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island in the strait, according to state TV.
American fighter jets struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm last Tuesday, according to a US military official.
'A solution can be found'
Washington announced what it called an "economic asphyxiation" campaign on Iran in August aimed at curbing its trade and financial flows.
Gharibabadi said Saturday, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency, that "we consider the economic blockade an act of war and we will take all necessary measures to lift it".
"We have made this known to the other parties, including the mediators", he added, saying "the United States was aware of this."
In an interview published on Saturday by the state-run Iran Daily newspaper, Araghchi reiterated that Tehran would not allow its stockpiles of enriched uranium to leave the country.
The Iranian nuclear programme is one of the major issues in Iranian-American relations. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Tehran insists the programme is entirely civilian in nature.
"I believe a solution can be found, but we have clear red lines: the material will not be taken out of the country," Araghchi said.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said US and Israeli strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure had exacerbated energy problems "and we should therefore expect difficulties this winter".
Mohammad Allahdad, head of Iran's national electricity company, told state TV that the country will impose rolling power cuts from Sunday.
"Given the country's fuel supply conditions, the electricity sector will be forced to impose distribution restrictions," he said.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he hurled a throw-in into the fac
items.text:
Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after throwing a ball into an opponent’s face as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.
Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he hurled a throw-in into the face of Columbus forward Gonzalo Tapia, with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.
Messi and Tapia were both shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards that the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.
“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said at a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.”
Chapman later defended his decision to show Messi only a yellow card.
“The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter.
Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were trailing 1-0 after an early penalty from the Chile international Tapia.
The reigning MLS champions went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Taha Habroune doubling Columbus’s lead shortly after half-time before Tapia added his second at Miami’s Nu Stadium.
The result means seventh-seeded Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in Game 2 of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.
“It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily González said afterwards.
“We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out.
“There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.”
FC Dallas 3-0 Portland Timbers
Joaquín Valiente scored twice in the space of two minutes as FC Dallas beat the Portland Timbers 3-0 in the opening game of their best-of-three Western Conference first-round series.
The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute, volleying home a rebound after Daniel Job’s shot was parried by Portland goalkeeper James Pantemis.
Valiente doubled the lead two minutes later, timing his run to meet another pass from Job before redirecting the ball between Pantemis’s legs.
Samuel Sarver completed the scoring in the fourth minute of stoppage time, finishing a cross from Logan Farrington on the counterattack.
Dallas goalkeeper Daniel de Sousa Britto, known simply as Daniel, made four saves, while Pantemis finished with five for Portland.
The Timbers also lost Ariel Lassiter to an apparent injury in the 33rd minute.
Second-seeded Dallas can advance to the Western Conference semi-finals with a victory in Portland next Saturday.
New England Revolution 2-0 Philadelphia Union
Teenager Peyton Miller scored one goal and helped create another as the New England Revolution beat the Philadelphia Union 2-0 in the opening game of their Eastern Conference first-round series.
The 19-year-old Miller became the fifth-youngest goalscorer in MLS Cup playoffs history when he volleyed home a cross from Jack Harrison in the 73rd minute, his effort bouncing off the crossbar and into the net.
New England had taken the lead in the 10th minute when Miller’s shot from the edge of the penalty area deflected off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel for an own goal.
Harrison, who came on as a substitute in the 62nd minute, was making his first appearance since 9 September after missing more than two months with a quadriceps injury.
Philadelphia nearly equalized in the 37th minute when Cavan Sullivan turned and fired a shot from outside the penalty area that struck the left post.
The Union fielded the youngest starting lineup in MLS Cup playoffs history, with an average age of 23 years and 207 days, breaking the record set by the New York Red Bulls in 2022.
Matt Turner made two saves to preserve the shutout for New England, who can advance to the Eastern Conference semi-finals with a victory in Philadelphia next Saturday.

items.text:
Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least 24 in Nigeria
Police say the boat driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.
A boat believed to be carrying hundreds of attendees to a funeral has overturned in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people, according to authorities.
The overcrowded vessel capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure while travelling from the communities of Ayama to Ukubie, according to police.
“So far, 24 bodies have been recovered from the scene of the incident, while search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for the National Emergency Management Agency, said on Saturday.
Rescue and search operations were continuing, he added.
Two children were among the four bodies initially recovered from the water on Friday, police said at the time, adding that 24 people were rescued, with 19 treated at a local clinic and five taken to hospital in the state capital.
Police did not say how many people were on board, but some residents told the Reuters news agency there were at least 300.
Police said the driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.
According to a statement from the Bayelsa State Police Command, the accident occurred at the river junction between the Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, in the state’s Southern Ijaw district.
The boat that capsized was travelling “for a burial ceremony”, the statement also said, adding that police are “coordinating efforts with local divers and other responders”.
Such boat accidents are common on Nigeria’s busy rivers and waterways, often caused by overloaded vessels, poor maintenance, or failure to comply with safety regulations.
A similar incident occurred in August, when at least 51 people died after a boat sank in northwest Nigeria’s Sokoto State. In another incident, in January, at least 26 people drowned after a boat ferrying people from Jigawa to Yobe State capsized.

Displaced Palestinians protest as Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza
Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings as part of a ‘gradual displacement’ policy, a Gaza mayor says.
Hundreds of displaced Palestinians have protested as Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings in Gaza, beyond the line they withdrew to under last year’s ceasefire.
Al Jazeera journalist Moath al-Kahlout, reporting from Gaza’s Deir el-Balah, said displaced Palestinians who live in the area near the “Yellow Line” gathered on Saturday to demonstrate against Israel’s intensifying air strikes.
The “Yellow Line” separates Israeli- and Hamas-controlled areas in Gaza since the “ceasefire” signed in October 2025.
“More than 500 housing units have been destroyed in less than a month,” said Mohammed Musleh, mayor of Deir-el Balah’s Maghazi municipality, told Al Jazeera.
“This is part of what appears to be a systematic policy of gradual creeping displacement aimed at forcing residents out of their camp and destroying as many homes as possible,” Musleh said.
Gaza’s Ministry of Public Works and Housing says 350,000 families are homeless after Israeli attacks destroyed 80 percent of the enclave’s homes.
Meanwhile, flooding in recent weeks devastated temporary tent housing, the ministry said.
The original “Yellow Line”, established under US President Donald Trump’s 20-point plan to end Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, marked the area to which Israeli forces initially withdrew. They were expected to make further withdrawals gradually, but instead seized more territory.
“If we go back to October 2025, when the ceasefire was signed, the ‘Yellow Line’ was much further east,” al-Kahlout said.
Now, nearly two-thirds of Gaza is under Israeli army control or subject to access restrictions.
Rising death toll
Israeli attacks killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza on Saturday, including three who died when an Israeli drone struck a van delivering food aid to displaced people in Gaza City.
In the past 48 hours, Israeli strikes killed at least nine people, taking the death toll since the October 2025 “ceasefire” to 1,661, according to the latest report from Gaza’s Ministry of Health.
The ministry said 55 Palestinians were wounded in the past 48 hours, putting the total number of the wounded since October 2025 at 6,062.
More than 100 remains recovered
Gaza’s Civil Defence said on Saturday that its crew members recovered the bodies and remains of 129 people from 39 homes and other Israeli-destroyed buildings in the Nuseirat refugee camp, az-Zawayda and Deir el-Balah in central Gaza.
Rami al-Aidi, Civil Defence director in central Gaza, said 233 people had been reported missing beneath the rubble of those buildings.
The 53-day operation marked the conclusion of the second phase of a recovery project in central Gaza funded by the International Committee of the Red Cross.
Gaza’s Civil Defence said in October that about 8,000 bodies remained under the rubble across the enclave, including about 4,000 in Israeli-controlled areas. The agency warned that recovery could take eight to 10 years with the equipment available.

items.text:
COP31: UN Climate summit runs into second day of overtime
Published November 20, 2026last updated November 22, 2026
What you need to know
- Diplomats and delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey
- Like in previous years, the climate summit has been extended until a consensus is reached
- Peru blames 'geopolitical divisions' for lack of COP31 progress
- After a draft climate deal stripped all mentions of coal, oil, and gas, nations are bracing for another long night of negotiations
These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20 through Sunday, November 22:
We're pausing our coverage
As COP31 extends into a second day of overtime, we are pausing our coverage.
In the early hours of Sunday, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum informed delegates at a plenary that a third and "final" text would be sent to them for review.
He added that negotiators would have until 6:00 am (0400 GMT) "to come to us with agreement on the text" and that a closing plenary would then be convened at 9:00 am local time.
Stay tuned for more news in the coming hours.
IN DEPTH: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
The shift to green tech is already in full swing, including electric cars, electric buses, solar panels and heat pumps. But what is so electrifying about the latest wave of electrification?
Climate activist blames rich countries for COP failure
Harjeet Singh, the global convener of the Fill the Fund campaign and strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, said that COP31 could be a failure due to a lack of funding.
"COP31 is stuck for one simple reason: money. Europe and other rich countries came to Antalya with empty pockets," he wrote in a statement shared with multiple reporters.
"They've spent two weeks pushing electrification targets and demanding more ambition from developing countries, while refusing to pay for any of it," he added.
Singh accused wealthy countries of blocking a just transition mechanism and of ignoring calls to increase funding for the Adaptation Fund and the Loss and Damage Fund.
"You can't ask developing countries to transform their economies while they're drowning in disasters and debt," he wrote.
The climate activist stressed that the reason this COP failed wasn't a lack of solutions. It was due to "a lack of money and a lack of will from those who caused this crisis," he said.
IN DEPTH: Why is carbon capture not moving faster?
Carbon capture technology works, but its real-world capabilities are nowhere near to moving the needle on climate change. So what's the hold-up?
IN DEPTH: At COP31, conflict over climate science slows action on global warming
Attacks on climate science and disinformation seem to be delaying key decisions as the UN climate talks draw to a close in Antalya.
IN DEPTH: Africa at COP31 — Will climate cash finally flow?
Leaders from Africa, one of the continents worst hit by climate change, have spent years lobbying for hundreds of billions of dollars to help adapt to the rising impacts of global warming.
The rest of the world relies on African nations for their abundant natural resources, many of them used in clean energy production.
Yet at COP31, wealthy nations have so far failed to commit to the financing needed to help developing nations make a just transition.
Read our report from DW's Kathy Wood.
Peru blames 'geopolitical divisions' for lack of COP31 progress
The head of Peru's delegation at COP31, Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, warned that the UN climate summit was unlikely to end with a concrete deal on climate financing or cutting fossil fuel use.
Garrido Sanchez lamented that the outcome "would be very limited."
He reiterated how "geopolitical divisions" were stopping any final deal from mentioning reducing reliance on oil, gas and coal.
The Peruvian delegate singled out major oil producers, such as Gulf Arab states and Russia, as showing significant opposition.
He noted that while Latin American neighbor Panama had also signaled objection to including the term fossil fuels in the final text, Peru was "not so radical" and is keen to attract investment to "ensure our energy security" through renewables.
China throws weight behind '35-by-35' pledge
China has backed a plan proposed by COP host Turkey to raise global electricity demand to 35% by 2035 — up from the current 20%.
In a joint statement with Australia, which is leading negotiations between almost 200 nations at the COP31 summit in Turkey, Beijing said it welcomes "growing international ambition and cooperation ... to increase electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035 on a voluntary basis."
The statement goes on to highlight the benefits the transition can bring for the economy, jobs, energy security, public health and households.
The two partners also "acknowledge the importance of inclusive climate action that ensures no one is left behind," the text continued.
Dozens of countries, including EU states, Japan, South Korea and Canada, have so far signaled support for the voluntary goal, which aims to boost clean energy use.
Yet, environmental groups have warned that the draft text doesn't stipulate the use of solar, wind and other renewable energy sources, which could allow power plants using natural gas and coal to be included.
COP31: What to expect today
Good morning, and welcome back to DW's coverage of the UN's COP31 climate summit in Turkey.
Negotiators from nearly 200 countries worked through the night to finalize a deal, after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels — the leading cause of climate change.
COP31, being held in the Mediterranean city of Antalya, was due to wrap up on Friday, but has run over time amid deep divisions over fossil fuels.

items.title: Supersub Espí's 'most special' goal earns win for Madrid and praise from Nadal
items.summary:
MADRID -- Real Madrid supersub Carlos Espí said his 85th-minute winner against Celta Vigo was his "most special" goal yet for the club after earning his team all three points at the Bernabéu on Saturday.
Celta's Pablo Durán put the visitors ahead after just six minutes, before a late rally saw Jude
items.text:
MADRID -- Real Madrid supersub Carlos Espí said his 85th-minute winner against Celta Vigo was his "most special" goal yet for the club after earning his team all three points at the Bernabéu on Saturday.
Celta's Pablo Durán put the visitors ahead after just six minutes, before a late rally saw Jude Bellingham level for Madrid, and then Espí -- who was introduced on 79 minutes by coach José Mourinho -- score from close range, after Vinícius Júnior's cross, to seal a 2-1 victory.
- Madrid chief Pérez: "outrageous" that LaLiga president Tebas hasn't resigned
- Hunter: Has Vini Jr. finally put summer transfer saga behind him? Real Madrid need him at his best
Espí, 21, has played just 44 minutes for Madrid in LaLiga this season but he's now scored three, crucial goals to secure victories against Espanyol, Elche and Celta, as well as netting in the club's 4-3 Champions League comeback win away at Roma.
"I think it's the most special," Espí told reporters on Saturday, when asked about his first goal scored in front of the Bernabéu crowd.
"Honestly, it's a day I'll never forget ... I can't even count how many times I've dreamed of scoring here, celebrating with the fans, and hearing them chant my name."
Espí said coach Mourinho was "euphoric" after his late winner, and described meeting Rafael Nadal post-match, after the tennis legend was voted onto Madrid's board of directors earlier on Saturday.
"I went over to see [Nadal], and he was very proud of me," Espí said. "Having a legend like Rafa Nadal there, talking to me, it made me incredibly happy."
Mourinho cited the return from the international break as a factor in Madrid's lackluster first-half performance, which saw them trail at halftime.
"If you look at the big teams that played today: Arsenal didn't win, [Manchester] City didn't win, Chelsea didn't win, Bayern [Munich] didn't win," Mourinho said. "It's difficult."
Mourinho confirmed that Vinícius -- who he brought off the bench after 57 minutes on Saturday -- would start in Madrid's Champions League game with PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.
The coach also revealed why Espí is unlikely to start many games alongside first-choice center forward Kylian Mbappé.
"It's possible, but when we lose the ball, I -- on the touchline -- would have to run onto the pitch during the transition, and clatter someone on the opposing team," Mourinho joked.
"Playing with two pure forwards means your wingers have to be very capable of defending in central areas. And that wouldn't be Vinícius, for sure. Arda [Güler] might do it a bit, Brahim [Díaz] a bit, but given the characteristics of our wingers, we aren't built to play in a traditional 4-4-2."

Home defeats to big rivals. Injuries to key players. One of the worst defenses in the Premier League.
Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.
- Raya exits with injury as Arsenal held by Newcastle: 'Never good news'
- Man City at a crossroads as a sh
items.text:
Home defeats to big rivals. Injuries to key players. One of the worst defenses in the Premier League.
Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.
- Raya exits with injury as Arsenal held by Newcastle: 'Never good news'
- Man City at a crossroads as a shell of themselves
- VAR review: Should Haaland's goal vs Fulham have been disallowed
"We're in a fragile moment," Alonso said Saturday after seeing his team overrun in a 4-1 home loss to Leeds, who hadn't won at Stamford Bridge this century.
"We need to be tougher," he added. "It's something mandatory in this competition.
Already without major players in striker João Pedro and defender Maxence Lacroix because of injuries, Chelsea fell apart against Leeds following the enforced withdrawal of Moisés Caicedo in the 22nd minute after the Ecuador midfielder landed awkwardly on his back while making a challenge.
Despite going ahead within three minutes through Emmanuel Emegha on his first start, Leeds equalized almost immediately through Noah Okafor and dominated the second half, scoring through Dominic Calvert-Lewin -- via the penalty spot -- Okafor again and then U.S. midfielder Brenden Aaronson.
Leeds -- whose rivalry with Chelsea dates back to the 1960s and early '70s -- last beat the London club away in 1999. Less than a month ago, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018. Before the international break, Chelsea lost 1-0 at Sunderland, which started that match in last place.
Chelsea, one of the biggest spenders in Europe in recent seasons, has tumbled toward midtable and are putting in lethargic performances even though the team doesn't have the hindrance of European competition this season.
"After we lost Moises, we lost completely the momentum," Alonso said. "Until then we were doing OK, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing. After that, we never got the good feeling and were not able to come from the pressure. It completely changed.
"I'm not feeling [let down]. We do it as a team, as [a] collective. We need to support each other. We need to find solutions to do better because this will happen. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. But the physicality, the duels, it's not the only explanation. The mentality part we can do better."
Chelsea has now conceded 20 goals in 11 games, with only last-place Crystal Palace and promoted teams Ipswich and Coventry letting in more.
Information from The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.

items.title: Milan boss Amorim heaps praise on Pulisic: 'The player we cannot replace'
items.summary:
AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has heaped praise on Christian Pulisic, calling him "the player we cannot replace."
The 28-year-old is in sparkling form, having scored three goals in two games for the United States men's national team -- including a stunning bicycle kick -- and three in four in Ser
items.text:
AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has heaped praise on Christian Pulisic, calling him "the player we cannot replace."
The 28-year-old is in sparkling form, having scored three goals in two games for the United States men's national team -- including a stunning bicycle kick -- and three in four in Serie A prior to the international break.
"I can tell you today that Pulisic, maybe, is the player that we cannot replace," Amorim told a news conference ahead of Milan's game against Frosinone on Sunday.
"The characteristics of turning between the lines, we don't have another Pulisic. There are some moments in Europe, in this last schedule, we had to save -- a little bit -- Pulisic.
"There is nothing that I can say better than saying that Pulisic has some characteristics that, if we don't have it on the pitch, the team feels a lot that Pulisic is not there. From that, you can understand how important Pulisic is for us.
"He's not that kind of guy that speaks a lot, but [he] speaks on the pitch, without speaking. He wants the ball all the time and you can feel it against Genoa. If you see all the plays, Pulisic is the guy that pulls the team up. Him and [Adrien] Rabiot."
The former Borussia Dortmund and Chelsea winger has been with the Italian club since 2023 and recently signed a new deal through 2031.
"I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club," Amorim said on Saturday.
"I think [that] was clear [when] the club showed him a new contract. That helps always a player."

The Portuguese coach added: "When he was not playing [at the beginning of this season], I said 'Pulisic is really important for us.'
"But we cannot forget the injuries, the way we need to build the player in order to [suit] the context."
Milan sit in fifth place in Serie A with seven wins from 11 games. Sunday's opponents Frosinone are one of the surprise packages of the season so far and are just one place below the Rossoneri.

The defending champions' 12th straight win in all competitions was soured by yet another injury.
"We will have to wait until
items.text:
Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué was carried off on a stretcher with a serious knee injury late in the first half of the team's 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday.
The defending champions' 12th straight win in all competitions was soured by yet another injury.
"We will have to wait until tomorrow to know the exact nature of the injury. But it is a serious injury, we have seen the images," PSG coach Luis Enrique said after the game. "That's the life of a professional footballer, you have to realize that this is part of a career and you have to accept it."
It happened when he turned to shield the ball from Nice midfielder Sofiane Diop and his fully-extended leg buckled under him without any contact from Diop.
The France forward fell to the ground clutching his right knee in the 39th minute and looked in severe pain as he cried out. Moments later he was taken off on a stretcher and placed both hands on his face.
"He is sad and worried," Luis Enrique said. "He will come back twice as strong, I have no doubt."
The 21-year-old Doué -- who shot to prominence with an outstanding performance in the 2025 Champions League win against Inter Milan -- had scored his second league goal of the season earlier in the first half.
Spain forward Ferran Torres replaced him and scored the third goal. Senny Mayulu got PSG's opening goal.
Two-time defending champions PSG face Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Doué missed stretches of last season with a calf strain and a thigh injury and had a bothersome ankle injury the previous season.
His latest injury is a concern for Enrique, after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore the ACL in his right knee against Barcelona on Oct. 20 and Ousmane Dembélé and captain Marquinhos tore thigh muscles in that game.
Dembélé came off the bench against Nice in the second half for PSG.
Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

David Raya was forced off with an injury during Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Saturday.
The Spain goalkeeper walked off holding his left arm and looked in discomfort as he did so. He was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.
"Unfortunately, he had to come off which is never good news," Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said. "He will get assessed now and he will probably have an MRI tomorrow to see what it is exactly because at the moment I don't know.
"It was a knock. I don't know how it happened or what the injury is at the moment so we'll have to see wait and see tomorrow.
"We know how important David is for us but tomorrow we will have more news."
The 31-year-old had played every minute of Arsenal's Premier League and Champions League games this season up to that point.
He also played 37 out of Arsenal's 38 games as they lifted the Premier League last season.
Raya has won the league's Golden Glove award in each of the last three seasons, and Arsenal have conceded the joint-fewest goals so far this Premier League season.
The Spaniard could join Bukayo Saka and Martín Zubimendi on the sidelines, although Saturday's game did see William Saliba feature in a Premier League squad for the first time this season.

Arsenal opened the scoring through Eberechi Eze on Saturday but found themselves behind midway through the second half thanks to goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw, before Noni Madueke rescued a point for the visitors.
The result saw Arteta's side go six points clear at the top of the table.

items.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?

items.text:
Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
- Published
Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.
At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40.
He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections.
"Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC.
But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.
Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.
The current president, Bola Tinubu, is 74 and would be 79 by the end of a second term if he is re-elected in January.
His main challengers are also considerably older. Atiku Abubakar, seeking the presidency for the seventh time, is 79, while Peter Obi is 65.
Of the 18 presidential candidates, only one is under 40 - Moses Olusoji Adebisi, a 35-year-old businessman representing the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA).
Although he says he is confident of winning, few Nigerians appear to know much about him and he has not been seen much on the campaign trail.
The contrast is striking in a country with one of the world's youngest populations, where young people have repeatedly demonstrated their ability to shape political debate and mobilise for change.
In the previous election, Obi, then 61, galvanised millions of young Nigerians through a social media-driven movement known as the "Obedients".
His campaign promised a break from the established political order, appealing particularly to young people struggling to find jobs and earn a decent living.
But his failure to win the presidency left many of his supporters disillusioned.
"At the time we were so hopeful, but unfortunately the result wasn't what we wanted, which made many lose hope in the system," former Obedient Nonso Chukwudi tells the BBC.
The movement had built on the momentum of the EndSars protests in 2020, which grew into one of Nigeria's biggest youth-led movement in decades.
Initially sparked by anger over police brutality, the demonstrators developed into a wider call for political reform, accountability and greater youth participation in governance.
But the protests were eventually crushed by the authorities. About 56 were reportedly killed, although officials dispute this figure, while hundreds were arrested and some had their bank accounts frozen.
Both EndSars and the Obedients demonstrated the capacity of young Nigerians to mobile around political causes.
But turning that enthusiasm into sustained electoral participation has proved much harder.
Hajara Musa, 33, is among those who have lost faith in the political system. She has no plans to register or vote in the near future.
"I just feel like things are already determined and I'll just be wasting my time. It is going to be the same people all over again," she tells the BBC.
The electoral register appears to reflect this growing disillusionment.
Although the number of registered voters has increased by 10 million to over 103 million since the last election, enrolment of those under 35 has actually fallen, by about seven million.
Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023.
Nigeria's electoral commission, Inec, says it has made efforts to encourage more young people to register ahead of the 2027 general elections.
This includes appointing nine ambassadors from the entertainment industry, spanning film, music and comedy, to reach younger audiences.
But the figures suggest these efforts have yet to make a significant difference.
Dalhatu says he understands the frustration but argues that young Nigerians cannot expect change, if they stay away from the political process.
"Unfortunately, many prefer to just post on social media" instead of getting involved, he says.
Of course being young does not mean you are necessarily the best candidate.
For those who want to participate, there is a formidable obstacle to getting into politics - money.
Dalhatu dreams of becoming president one day, but says he has previously had to abandon campaigns because he could not raise enough funds.
The cost of running for office in Nigeria is notoriously high.
Under the Electoral Act, presidential candidates were allowed to spend up to 5bn naira (£2.8m; $3.7m) on campaigns ahead of the 2023 elections. That spending limit has since been doubled.
The cost of nomination forms alone puts the presidency beyond the reach of most aspiring young Nigerians.
The ruling All Progressive Congress (APC), along with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) have each set their presidential nomination fee at 100m naira ($74,000; £56,000), making it extremely hard for new challengers to emerge.
Since the return to democracy in 1999, only two parties have governed Nigeria - the PDP from 1999 to 2015 and the APC since 2015.
These parties, alongside the ADC, formed last year by politicians who had defected from the other two, have established nationwide network of branches, supporters and campaigners.
Those aspiring candidates without the financial resources to secure nomination forms and compete in the internal party contests of the main parties have little chances of becoming president.
The barriers are also evident in the National Assembly.
Not one of Nigeria's 109 senators is under 40, while only 14 of the 360 members of the House of Representatives fall into that age group.
"I have been in politics for many years and I will tell you that young people in this country lack the resources to become president," says Dalhatu, who is running under Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress.
Fatima Zahra Umar, a young politician in the APC who has previously tried to run for a seat in the House of Representatives, agrees.

"So far, 24 bodies have been recovered from the scene of the incident, while search and rescue operations are ongoing," sa
items.text:
Nigeria: At least 24 dead after boat capsizes
November 22, 2026
A boat capsized in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people, the country's emergency agency said on Saturday.
"So far, 24 bodies have been recovered from the scene of the incident, while search and rescue operations are ongoing," said Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for the National Emergency Management Agency.
The boat was carrying mourners for a burial ceremony from the town of Ayama to Ukubie in the southern Bayelsa State on Friday when it sank.
Boat reportedly suffered mechanical failure
Authorities have not confirmed how many passengers were on board.
"Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way," Nigerian President Bola Tinubu said in a statement on X.
Two children were among the four bodies initially recovered from the water on Friday, when 24 survivors were rescued, according to police.
Police spokesman Musa Mohammed said that preliminary reports suggested that the boat suffered a mechanical problem.
Deadly boat mishaps in Nigeria
Boat accidents are common on Nigeria's busy river networks. Overloading, poor vessel maintenance, and failure to comply with safety norms usually cause them.
In August, at least 51 died after a boat capsized in northwest Nigeria's Sokoto State.
In September 2025, a boat carrying over 100 passengers sank in north-central Niger State, leaving dozens dead.

items.title: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
items.summary:
Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
Joseph Aoun says ‘two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked’ mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withd
items.text:
Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
Joseph Aoun says ‘two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked’ mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withdrawal from his country’s south.
In a speech on Saturday, on the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun said Lebanon faces two interconnected fateful tests: the “Israeli occupation of parts of our land” and “foreign interference” from “some influential parties in the Iranian regime” through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state.
These “two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked” mean that Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence, he added.
“Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks. And return our captives,” Aoun demanded of Israel.
Dozens of Lebanese citizens are believed to be held in Israeli detention centres, including civilians as well as members of the Hezbollah armed group captured during fighting in southern Lebanon.
The president also pledged to press ahead with plans to bring all weapons under state control, declaring that there would be “no weapons outside the state that take orders from, or serve the interests of foreign powers.”
“You must hand over your weapons,” Aoun said.
Lebanon’s government has promised to disarm Hezbollah, the Iran-backed Lebanese group whose arsenal has long outstripped that of the national army and that has justified its weapons as necessary to resist Israel.
Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement in June, following US-mediated talks, which included the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanese territories and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.
But implementation has stalled, with Hezbollah refusing to surrender its weapons and Israel continuing to strike Lebanon.
Israeli strikes
On Saturday, Israeli strikes hit the districts of Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun in southern Lebanon.
Al Jazeera correspondents reported that one of the air strikes hit the outskirts of Baraachit, a town in Bint Jbeil.
They said Baraachit came under Israeli gunfire at dawn and reported the movement of Israeli military vehicles on the outskirts of the town.
Israeli warplanes launched a second missile attack on the town of Kfar Tebnit in Nabatieh, after the first failed to detonate, according to Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA).
The NNA reported that Israeli forces carried out three explosions in Wadi al-Khiam in the Marjayoun district, but gave no further details.
Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon have killed at least 4,386 people and wounded 12,407 others since March 2, when the latest Hezbollah-Israel war started.
Lebanon’s Ministry of Health said that since Israel began its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, Israeli strikes in Lebanon have killed 8,953 people and injured 30,643 others.

France book South Africa rematch in Nations Championship final with bonus-point victory over Argentina
France beat Argentina 45-17, securing the bonus-point victory they needed to reach the final of the Nations Championship; France will meet South Africa in the November 29 final at Twickenham; France beat the Springboks 21-19 last week in Paris
Last Updated: 21/11/26 11:34pm
France reached the Nations Championship final after beating Argentina 45-17 with seven tries on Saturday.
England's 37-12 win against New Zealand left France needing a bonus-point victory to make the November 29 final against South Africa, who topped the southern hemisphere group despite losing to Ireland.
Already leading 21-10, Emilien Gailleton got France's fourth try for the bonus point in the 64th minute against 14 men, and moments later the yellow card for Pumas prop Mayco Vivas was upgraded to red.
France finished with three more tries. Lock Tyler Duguid charged through following an attacking lineout, centre Kalvin Gourgues showed stunning pace from near halfway to make the left corner, and Louis Bielle-Biarrey completed the rout with his 31st try in 30 tests.
In the first half lock Mickaël Guillard and try-scoring hooker Peato Mauvaka crossed for France. Returning fly-half Matthieu Jalibert cleverly set up silky centre Gourgues shortly after the break for the first of his two tries.
Argentina led briefly at 10-7 for 10 minutes thanks to a converted try from centre Justo Piccardo and a penalty from fly-half Tomas Albornoz.
Jalibert's faster than expected recovery from a torn thigh allowed captain Antoine Dupont to resume at scrum-half after wearing the No 10 jersey a week ago against South Africa.
Dupont showed his class at the end with a kick down the left flank for Bielle-Biarrey's try.
Gourdes nailed five conversions as a makeshift kicker on the night.
Tributes were held before the game for Federico Martín Aramburú, the former Argentina player who died four years ago after being fatally shot in Paris.

items.text:
Grand Slam of Darts: Michael van Gerwen proves he is still a force to be reckoned with after reaching semi-finals
Debutant Kevin Doets faces three-time champion Gerwyn Price in the first semi-final before Michael van Gerwen and Gian van Veen renew their rivalry on the big stage; watch the climax of the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports
Saturday 21 November 2026 23:25, UK
Michael van Gerwen has shown he is still a force to be reckoned with as he prepares to face fellow Dutchman Gian van Veen in his first major semi-final in over a year.
With Luke Littler and Luke Humphries already at home, Van Gerwen will be looking to get his hands on some TV silverware for the first time since the 2025 World Series of Darts Finals.
Van Gerwen, who threw perfection in the opening leg against Tom Sykes to record his first televised nine-darter on Sky Sports in 14 years, takes on Van Veen on Sunday, with debutant Kevin Doets going head-to-head with three-time champion Gerwyn Price in the first semi-final.
- MVG stars in Grand Slam epic clash with TWO nine-darters
- Price survives last-leg thriller against Springer to set up Doets semi-final
- Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results
- Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW
"There has been a lot of criticism about me in the last couple of years, and rightly so, because I wasn't performing. Then you need to make sure you pull your finger out," said Van Gerwen, who traded nine-darters with Sykes on a historic night in Wolverhampton.
"To reach the semi-final is nice, but then to also do it the way I did it today.
"This means the world to me. It has been a battle; I have to work hard, I know that, but then to also show it, it's magnificent.
"I have been feeling good, and to also produce what I am doing, I hope I can do even more later in the tournament. I am feeling good, and when I feel good, I can do anything; I know that.
"I showed some real class and some real ability, and moving on that gives me goosebumps, that gives me the energy, and I hope I can show more tomorrow."
Van Veen defeated 2022 runner-up Nathan Aspinall in a bruising battle to set up a meeting against his Dutch compatriot.
"As a Dutchman, a Grand Slam semi-final against Michael is always a dream coming true, but as you said, the way he played today, it was phenomenal," admitted the former European champion.
"If he does that on Sunday, I'm going to be in a whole lot of trouble, but hopefully he doesn't, and hopefully I'll step up my game and then it's going to be a totally different game and very close.
"Michael played phenomenal. Fair play to him, but as I said, it's going to be a totally different game on Sunday and hopefully I'll be ready.
"I just have to take it game-by-game.
"I will put 100 per cent focus in that semi-final and then as soon as I hopefully get that job done, then we will worry about the final.
"If you worry already about the final before the semi, you might lose quite convincingly."
'Michael's going to be feeling really good, and that's the problem for Gian'
Three-time world champion John Part speaking on Sky Sports:
"Michael has handled Gian well this year. He hasn't dropped a match to him. There's been nothing really hugely consequential about any of the matches they played.
"Michael's going to be feeling really good and that's the problem for Gian.
"He's going to have to come out, grind into the match, but he'll hopefully want to spark into the flowing, really better average stuff, the A-game type stuff.
"That was pretty good quality overall for the length of format tonight, but he'll think, ' oh, I can do so much better'. And he'll want to. And against Michael, who better to do it against."
Is Doets a champion in waiting?
Price will take on Doets with the Welshman into an eighth successive televised semi-final at the PDC this year, although he has yet to break his duck and is without a major victory since 2022.
'The Iceman' is chasing a fourth Grand Slam title and first in five years, but Dutchman Doets is enjoying a brilliant breakout season, claiming his first senior PDC title at Players Championship 13 in May before reaching his maiden European Tour final at the Austrian Darts Open.
He powered past Jermaine Wattimena to reach his first televised PDC semi-final, with his red-hot form impressing Wayne Mardle.
"Kevin Doets won 11 of the last 13 legs against an opponent averaging a ton. That's how good he is," said Mardle.
"I feel really strongly about Kevin Doets' future.
"It wouldn't surprise me if he deals with Gerwyn Price and goes on and wins it.
"He's playing so well so often, and you've got to play good enough often enough, and he does.
"He's a champion in waiting."

items.text:
Nations Championship: Wales fall short in 29-26 defeat to Australia after epic New Zealand victory
Australia narrowly defeated Wales at the Principality stadium in Cardiff; Wales couldn't follow up the previous week's epic victory over New Zealand, their first over the All Blacks since 1953; Wales to face Japan on Finals Weekend with Australia taking on Ireland
Last Updated: 21/11/26 11:00pm
Wales failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand as Australia edged their Nations Championship match 29-26 in Cardiff.
A first victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to week-long celebrations in Wales.
But Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three on the spin for the first time since the 2023 World Cup.
Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot.
Wales also scored four tries through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions, but fell agonisingly short.
Australia fly-half Carter Gordon scored a penalty in the 74th minute to give the Wallabies a 29-21 lead, which proved enough for victory despite Wales securing a fourth try through replacement hooker Elias two minutes from time.
Wales battled for the winning score in a dramatic close to the match but their attempt to go the length of the field was ended when the ball was knocked on.
"Wales are a tough outfit. What a match," Ikitau said after he was awarded player of the match.
"It's been a tough couple of weeks for us. I know the heart's always there but when you don't get the results it's pretty disheartening. I'm proud of the boys and proud of the effort today."

items.title: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
items.summary:
Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that th
items.text:
Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to a new executive order.
The companies must also coordinate with the White House and U.S. agencies on "appropriate responses" to any such requests, the order issued late Friday says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.
The order is the Republican administration's latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January. Democrats have made government contracts one of their top investigative targets, noting that federal money has been flowing to companies linked with Trump's family, particularly at the Pentagon.
White House officials have already begun taking steps to exert more control over how agencies and officials respond to congressional requests, anticipating there will be a flood of investigations initiated by Democrats.
Trump's counsel, Will Scharf, told federal agencies on Monday that they must seek approval from his office and the White House's Office of Legislative Affairs before agreeing to appear before Congress. Scharf also suggested in a recent letter to Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, that some congressional investigations may amount to "blatant criminality."
Garcia sent letters this week directing members of Trump's family and top administration officials to preserve documents. Scharf sought to dismiss the requests, noting in a letter to Democratic lawmakers that they are not yet in the majority and cannot compel compliance.
Responding to the new executive order, Garcia said it was part of the administration's "blatant attack on Congress' constitutional right to conduct oversight." He said that despite efforts to impede investigations, "we're just getting started."
In a fact sheet, the White House framed the new requirements as "protecting executive privileges from congressional overreach," arguing that some congressional leaders have tried to intrude on executive branch privileges by "harassing private companies that contract with the federal government."
Presidents of both parties have long used executive privilege to resist congressional inquiries, but the claims can set up messy, protracted legal fights as parties dispute whether it applies. Executive privilege allows the president to keep information from the courts, Congress and the public to protect the confidentiality of White House deliberations, but the protection is far from absolute.
The latest executive order applies to all contractors and subcontractors, a universe of tens of thousands of businesses.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full-debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich.

After De Zerbi revealed Williams-Barnett prepared for the match on the team bus by watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, he said: "Luca is a special player.
"I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top team-mates.
"I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.
"The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.
"And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.
"Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch."
Asked if Williams-Barnett can reach the level of Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi said: "Yes, I think so.
"And one of the best things in my career… I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.
"I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?"
Who is Williams-Barnett?
Williams-Barnett joined Tottenham as a 10-year-old from Luton, his home town, and has been in the Spurs academy since.
There has been plenty of hype around the winger, whose talent was noticeable when he won the U18 Premier League goal of the season award for a long-range stunner against Leicester.
The teenager then began featuring in Spurs' first-team squads, but after being named on the bench for a handful of games in the 2024/25 season, Williams-Barnett was finally handed his debut in September 2025 by then-boss Thomas Frank as he came on as a substitute in the Carabao Cup third-round home win over Doncaster.
Eight days later, Williams-Barnett signed his first professional contract with Spurs at the age of 17.
His appearance against Doncaster proved to be his only first-team action last season as he hit a hat-trick against Leicester for Tottenham U21s before netting five goals in a win over Slavia Prague for Spurs' academy team in a UEFA Youth League game.
He was deservedly rewarded by De Zerbi for a fine youth season by playing a part in Tottenham's pre-season plans as he showed glimpses of his skill and quality during some run-outs.
But he has finally made his first-team breakthrough this season, and he should have had an assist on his Premier League debut in last month's win over Crystal Palace after he came on as a substitute to superbly tee up Mohammed Kudus, who somehow missed to add a third in the 2-0 win (watch below).

On the international stage, Williams-Barnett has represented England at all levels between U15s and U19s to date.
In September, he came on for Arsenal sensation Max Dowman to make his England U19 debut in a 1-0 win over the Republic of Ireland.
Tottenham and Arsenal have two of England's brightest prospects, and the pair could play major parts in north London derbies in the years to come.

items.summary:
Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
- Published
A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (£3,058).
The hair once belonged to John Gadsby, who entertained Washington in 1799 just before the latter's
items.text:
Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
- Published
A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (£3,058).
The hair once belonged to John Gadsby, who entertained Washington in 1799 just before the latter's death the same year, and was later obtained by a collector called John K Lattimer from a descendent of Gadsby's, according to Richmond Auctions, which sold the item.
Its new owner has not been named.
Saturday's sale is not the most expensive for Washington hair at auction. Three strands thought to have been removed from him close to or after his death stored in a locket sold for nearly $40,000 in 2021.
Gadsby, a resident of what in 1799 was the town of Alexandria in Virginia, entertained Washington for dinner shortly before his death later that year, according to a testament given in 1928 by Gadsby's granddaughter, Julia Ten Eyck McBlair, and which was posted on the Richmond Auctions website.
McBlair stated that her grandfather came into possession of Washington's hair "in view of the friendship and association with his last days" and had it framed and hung "under General Washington's portrait in our home in Washington City, there I have seen it all my life".
Gadsby hosted Washington's two birthday celebrations in 1798 and 1799, Richmond Auctions states.
Washington led American forces to victory against the British in the War of Independence and helped draft the US Constitution before becoming the country's first president in 1788. He stepped down in 1797 after serving two terms.
Several locks of Washington's hair have been preserved, including at least 50 examples that are in a collection at his former residence, Mount Vernon, which is now a museum.
"Public displays of hair from friends or loved ones peaked in the 19th century, but had long been popular among affluent families like the Washingtons," a blog on the Mount Vernon website states.
As well as lockets of his hair, other items associated with Washington have also done well at auction.
In July, a signed letter by Washington from 1776, in which he asks for soldiers for the Continental Army to fight the British, sold for $109,800.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability t
items.text:
Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.
Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”
“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”
Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.
That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”
